newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said two percent of the U.S. winter wheat cropwas harvested compared with seven percent a year ago and the five-year average of four percent.
In its weekly crop progress report, USDA said three percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in very poor condition, nine percent poor, 28 percent fair, 49 percent good and 11 percent excellent.
In the report on conditions for the week ended June 8, USDA one percent of the U.S. corn crop was in very poor condition, four percent poor, 30 percent fair, 55 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
It said 84 percent of the U.S. soybean crop was planted compared with 57 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 70 percent.
The department reported one percent of the U.S. cotton crop was in very poor condition, nine percent poor, 31 percent fair, 50 percent good and nine percent excellent.

USDA said 89 percent of the U.S. spring wheat crop had emerged compared with 76 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 88 percent. Sixty-nine percent of the crop was in good-to-excellent condition, the department said. -- Washington Commodities Desk (202) 898-8394
